raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Summary:
TensorBoard metrics cover device memory in six series but report nothing
host-side, so a run's CPU utilization and host resident memory are
invisible. That gap matters most for checkpointing: both the native DCP
`async_with_pinned_mem` stager and the torch_checkpointing backend stage
device state into pinned host memory, and pinned pages are resident by
definition, so a save can move host RSS by tens of GiB without moving any
device metric.

Add a `HostMonitor` alongside `DeviceMemoryMonitor`. Each rank measures its
current RSS, process-lifetime peak RSS, and process CPU time over the log
interval using `/proc/self/statm` and `resource.getrusage`. The current RSS
source has the same Linux semantics as `psutil.Process().memory_info().rss`
without adding a dependency.

TensorBoard normally records only one metrics rank, so local host values can
hide the worst rank at scale. Reduce the three samples over the world mesh and
emit:

    memory/host_rss_avg(GiB)             current RSS, rank average
    memory/host_rss_max(GiB)             current RSS, rank maximum
    memory/host_peak_rss_max(GiB)        lifetime RSS peak, rank maximum
    cpu/process_utilization_avg(%)       process CPU, rank average
    cpu/process_utilization_max(%)       process CPU, rank maximum

The CPU percentage sums CPU time across all process threads, so it can exceed
100%. The peak RSS metric uses a kernel high-water mark that is never reset,
which catches a staging buffer allocated and freed between log calls.

Test Plan:
`pytest -q tests/unit_tests/observability/test_host_monitor.py
tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_metrics_config.py tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py`
passes 19 tests, including a real two-rank Gloo reduction test.

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass for the two changed files. A direct
Pyrefly check of `torchtitan/components/metrics.py` reports zero errors. The
whole-project Pyrefly hook still reports four unrelated missing `attn_gym`
imports in Kimi K3 and Qwen3.5 files.

@@ -101,6 +109,100 @@ def build_device_memory_monitor():
     return device_memory_monitor
 
 
+# named tuple for passing host resource stats for logging
+HostStats = namedtuple(
+    "HostStats",
+    [
+        "rss_gib",
+        "max_rss_gib",
+        "cpu_utilization_pct",
+    ],
+)
+
+
+class HostMonitor:
+    """Tracks host resident memory and process CPU utilization.
+
+    Checkpoint staging copies device state into pinned host memory, and pinned
+    pages are resident by definition, so a save can move host RSS by tens of
+    GiB without moving any device metric. Everything here comes from the
+    standard library, so it adds no dependency.
+
+    ``max_rss_gib`` is a process-lifetime high-water mark that the kernel never
+    resets, unlike the device peaks which are reset after every log interval.
+    It is what catches a staging buffer that is allocated and freed entirely
+    between two log calls. It comes from different kernel accounting than
+    ``rss_gib``, so the two track each other without agreeing exactly, and the
+    peak can read marginally below the current value.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.page_size = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") if hasattr(os, "sysconf") else 0
+        # ru_maxrss is KiB on Linux and bytes on macOS.
+        self._max_rss_scale = 1 if sys.platform == "darwin" else 1024
+        self._cpu_seconds_last_log = self._cpu_seconds()
+        self._time_last_log = time.perf_counter()
+
+    def _cpu_seconds(self) -> float:
+        usage = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF)
+        return usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime
+
+    def _rss_bytes(self) -> float:
+        # /proc is Linux-only; report -1 elsewhere rather than failing a run.
+        if not self.page_size:
+            return -1
+        try:
+            with open("/proc/self/statm") as f:
+                resident_pages = int(f.read().split()[1])
+        except (OSError, IndexError, ValueError):
+            return -1
+        return resident_pages * self.page_size
+
+    def get_stats(self) -> HostStats:
+        now = time.perf_counter()
+        cpu_seconds = self._cpu_seconds()
+        time_delta = now - self._time_last_log
+        # Sums CPU time across every thread, so this exceeds 100% whenever the
+        # process has more than one runnable thread.
+        cpu_utilization_pct = (
+            100 * (cpu_seconds - self._cpu_seconds_last_log) / time_delta
+            if time_delta > 0
+            else 0.0
+        )
+        self._cpu_seconds_last_log = cpu_seconds
+        self._time_last_log = now
+
+        max_rss = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+        return HostStats(
+            _to_gib(self._rss_bytes()),
+            _to_gib(max_rss * self._max_rss_scale),
+            cpu_utilization_pct,
+        )
+
+
+def _reduce_host_stats(
+    local_stats: HostStats, world_mesh: DeviceMesh
+) -> tuple[HostStats, HostStats]:
+    """Return the world-wide average and maximum for each host statistic."""

+class HostMonitor:
+    """Tracks host resident memory and process CPU utilization.
+
+    Checkpoint staging copies device state into pinned host memory, and pinned
+    pages are resident by definition, so a save can move host RSS by tens of
+    GiB without moving any device metric. Everything here comes from the
+    standard library, so it adds no dependency.
+
+    ``max_rss_gib`` is a process-lifetime high-water mark that the kernel never
+    resets, unlike the device peaks which are reset after every log interval.
+    It is what catches a staging buffer that is allocated and freed entirely
+    between two log calls. It comes from different kernel accounting than
+    ``rss_gib``, so the two track each other without agreeing exactly, and the
+    peak can read marginally below the current value.

+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.page_size = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") if hasattr(os, "sysconf") else 0
+        self.host_capacity_gib = (
+            _to_gib(self.page_size * os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES"))
+            if self.page_size
+            else -1.0
+        )
+        # ru_maxrss is KiB on Linux and bytes on macOS.
+        self._max_rss_scale = 1 if sys.platform == "darwin" else 1024
+        self._cpu_seconds_last_log = self._cpu_seconds()
+        self._time_last_log = time.perf_counter()
+
+    def _cpu_seconds(self) -> float:
+        usage = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF)
+        return usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime
+
+    def _rss_bytes(self) -> float:

+        if not self.page_size:
+            return -1
+        try:
+            with open("/proc/self/statm") as f:
+                resident_pages = int(f.read().split()[1])
+        except (OSError, IndexError, ValueError):
+            return -1
+        return resident_pages * self.page_size
+

+        now = time.perf_counter()
+        cpu_seconds = self._cpu_seconds()
+        time_delta = now - self._time_last_log

+        # process has more than one runnable thread.
+        cpu_utilization_pct = (
+            100 * (cpu_seconds - self._cpu_seconds_last_log) / time_delta
+            if time_delta > 0
+            else 0.0
+        )
+        self._cpu_seconds_last_log = cpu_seconds
+        self._time_last_log = now
+

+        return HostStats(
